passage:
Counsellor's note, written by Shalini.
Lalremsiami, Class 10, wants to take the arts stream and apply to a design course. Her family has planned science and medical coaching. She told me she fears being called selfish and letting everyone down, and she has not raised it at home. She spoke clearly about her reasons: a portfolio she has already started, a design college she has read about, and how she would support the family later.
I did not choose for her. I asked her to write her reasons on one page and offered to invite her parents to a meeting where they could share their own thoughts too. They came on Friday. Her father asked many questions and said he would visit the design college with her.

qa.q: Which stream does Lalremsiami want to take?
qa.a: Lalremsiami wants to take the arts stream.

qa.q: What is Lalremsiami afraid of, according to the note?
qa.a: She fears being called selfish and letting everyone down.

qa.q: What steps did Shalini take that respected both Lalremsiami and her family?
qa.a: Shalini asked Lalremsiami to write her reasons on one page and invited her parents to a meeting where they could share their thoughts as well.

qa.q: How did Lalremsiami's father respond at the meeting?
qa.a: Her father asked many questions and said he would visit the design college with her, which shows he was willing to listen and look.

grounding: A teenager wants a stream different from the family plan and fears being called selfish; explaining goals and inviting family thoughts respects both.

passage:
Sunday night. Papa's plan is commerce, so I can join the shop later. I want science and then biology. Every time I try to say it, the word "selfish" comes up in my head, as if wanting my own path means not caring about the family. Sangeeta, my older cousin, who took a different stream herself, says the wish itself isn't selfish. She told me to be clear, not loud.
So this is my plan. I will write down my reasons on one page: what I like about biology, what I could do with it, how I would still help at the shop on holidays. Then I will ask everyone to sit after dinner on Friday and tell me what they think. I want to hear them too.
Irawati

qa.q: Who told Irawati to be clear, not loud?
qa.a: Sangeeta, Irawati's older cousin, told Irawati to be clear, not loud.

qa.q: What is Irawati afraid of when trying to speak about the stream?
qa.a: Irawati is afraid of being called selfish, as if wanting a different path would mean not caring about the family.

qa.q: What is Irawati's plan for raising the subject at home?
qa.a: Irawati will write reasons on one page and ask everyone to sit after dinner on Friday, offering to help at the shop on holidays and listening to what they think.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta's own experience have helped Irawati?
qa.a: Sangeeta took a different stream herself, so she can show Irawati that wanting one's own path can be voiced without harming the family.

grounding: A teenager wants a stream different from the family plan and fears being called selfish, and plans to explain goals and hear the family.

passage:
In the school counsellor's office in Gangtok, Pema, sixteen, twisted her scarf. "My parents want science. My father's a doctor, my mother's a pharmacist. Everyone assumes I'll do medicine."
"And you?" asked Varun Sir.
"I want to study history. Maybe become a museum curator." She looked at the floor. "My aunt said wanting that is selfish when the family has built a clinic."
Varun Sir didn't laugh. "Wanting your own path isn't selfish. It's normal. What if you explained your goals to them, and asked what they think?"
"They'll be hurt."
"Maybe. But they'll be more hurt if you do medicine unhappily for ten years."
They made a plan together: Pema would research history courses and careers, then invite her parents to a meeting in this office to hear her reasons and share theirs.

qa.q: What does Pema want to become?
qa.a: Pema wants to study history and maybe become a museum curator.

qa.q: What is Pema afraid of?
qa.a: Pema is afraid of being called selfish and of hurting her parents, who expect her to do medicine.

qa.q: What plan did Pema and Varun Sir make, and why is it respectful?
qa.a: Pema will research history courses and careers and invite her parents to share their thoughts, respecting both her own goals and the family.

qa.q: How might Pema's parents feel hearing her plan?
qa.a: They may first feel surprised and disappointed, but hearing her reasons could help them understand her path.

grounding: A teenager wants a stream different from the family plan and fears being called selfish, and a counsellor helps her plan to explain her goals and invite her family's views.

passage:
Dear Arnab Uncle,
You always told me I could write to you about anything, so here it is.
Everyone in my family has done engineering. Appa, both my uncles, my cousin. It's decided that I'll take PCM next year. But I want to do commerce and study economics. I love how markets work; I read about it every night.
When I hinted at it, my grandmother said, "Only selfish boys go against the family." I haven't said anything since.
I'm not trying to hurt anyone. I just don't want to spend my life doing something I don't care about.
You studied economics even though your father wanted engineering. How did you tell him?
I want to explain my goals to Appa properly, not fight. Maybe I'll show him the courses and ask him what worries him.
Please write back soon.
Karthik

qa.q: What does Karthik want to study?
qa.a: Karthik wants to do commerce and study economics.

qa.q: How did Karthik feel after his grandmother's comment?
qa.a: Karthik felt hurt and afraid, and stayed silent after being called selfish.

qa.q: What is a wise way for Karthik to approach Appa?
qa.a: Karthik can explain his goals calmly, show the courses, and ask what worries Appa, which respects both his wishes and the family.

qa.q: How might Arnab Uncle feel reading Karthik's letter?
qa.a: Arnab Uncle might feel understanding and protective, remembering his own struggle to study economics.

grounding: A teenager wants a stream different from the family plan and fears being called selfish, and plans to explain his goals and invite his father's thoughts.

passage:
Kavitha, you remember I said I'd tell you how I ended up in journalism? Here's the story.
In Class 10, my whole family had one plan: science, then medicine, like my elder brother. When I said I wanted humanities, Ammi's sister said, "Salma is thinking only of herself. What about the family's name?"
I cried in the bathroom that night. I wanted to be a good daughter. But I also knew I loved writing more than anything.
So I didn't fight. I made a little file: my essays, the prize from the district competition, information about journalism courses and jobs. I sat with Abbu and Ammi on a Sunday and said, "I want to explain, and I want to hear what worries you."
Abbu worried about money. Ammi worried about safety. We talked for two hours. They agreed to humanities if I kept my marks up.
That's how Salma became a reporter, Kavitha.

qa.q: What did Salma put in her file?
qa.a: Salma put her essays, the prize from the district competition, and information about journalism courses and jobs.

qa.q: How was Salma feeling the night she cried in the bathroom?
qa.a: Salma felt torn and hurt, wanting to be a good daughter but loving writing more than anything.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Salma's story?
qa.a: Instead of fighting, she prepared a file and invited her parents to share their worries, which made them willing to agree.

qa.q: How might Abbu and Ammi have felt when Salma asked what worried them?
qa.a: They probably felt respected and listened to, which made it easier for them to share their fears about money and safety.

grounding: A teenager wants a different stream from the family plan and fears being called selfish, and explains her goals while inviting her family's views.

passage:
Sunday. At lunch Papa said the Class 11 form was due. "Science, obviously, like Sunaina Didi." Lokesh stirred his rasam and said nothing. That night he opened his sketchbook of bus-stop designs and felt like a traitor for wanting Humanities and design.
Wednesday. Lokesh asked Sunaina to sit with him and Papa after dinner. His hands were cold. "I don't want to be selfish," he said. "I want to show you why." He showed the sketchbook and a list of design colleges and jobs he had printed at the cyber cafe. "What do you both think I'm missing?" Papa asked about jobs after college. Sunaina asked about entrance exams.
Saturday. Papa came back from school with both forms. "Talk to your design teacher on Monday," he said. "Then we decide. Together."

qa.q: What did Lokesh show Papa and Sunaina on Wednesday?
qa.a: He showed his sketchbook and a list of design colleges and jobs.

qa.q: What was Lokesh feeling on Sunday night with the sketchbook?
qa.a: He felt guilty, almost like a traitor, for wanting Humanities and design instead of the family's plan.

qa.q: What made Wednesday's talk work?
qa.a: Lokesh explained his goal with real evidence and asked what they thought he was missing, which invited the family in rather than fighting them.

qa.q: How did Papa's view shift between Sunday and Saturday?
qa.a: On Sunday Papa assumed science was obvious, but by Saturday he brought both forms and asked Lokesh to see the design teacher first, treating it as a joint decision.

grounding: It illustrates a teenager who wants a stream different from the family plan, fears seeming selfish, and explains his goals while inviting family thoughts.
